context: A two-view linked visualization: a zoomable treemap (top, ~75% height) showing 66 food items across 7 groups sized by calories, linked to a parallel coordinates plot (bottom, 220px) spanning 6 nutrient dimensions (calories, protein, fat, carbs, fiber, sugar). Brushing on parcoords dims/highlights treemap cells; clicking a treemap group zooms into it.
first_impression: The treemap reads cleanly at a glance — group sizes immediately communicate caloric density — but the parallel coordinates panel feels cramped and tangled at rest.
what_works: The 7-category color palette stays just below the overload threshold and transfers coherently between both views, making it easy to match a treemap group to its parcoords lines without a legend lookup. The treemap zoom interaction reduces cognitive load by letting the viewer narrow focus to one group at a time, effectively turning 66 leaves into a smaller working set.
what_doesnt: The parcoords panel at 220px height is too shallow for 66 overlapping lines across 6 axes — at rest the lines form a dense tangle with no visible structure, and extreme outliers (Butter at 717 cal / 81g fat) compress the scales so that most items cluster indistinguishably near the bottom. The panel only becomes useful after brushing, but there is no affordance or prompt signaling that interaction is required.
